message.content:
The most well‑known dominant genetic trait in lions is the **presence of a mane in males**.  
A single dominant allele (often referred to as “M”) controls the development of the mane, so any male lion carrying at least one copy of this allele will grow a mane, while females (who are typically homozygous recessive for the trait) do not.
